# Why We're Changing How We Teach Maths

## What's Changing?

From next year, we're moving away from **streaming** (where students are separated into different classes based on ability) to **mixed-attainment teaching** (where students of different abilities learn together in the same class).

We know this might feel like a big change, so we want to explain why we're doing it.

---

## Why Make This Change?

### It helps more students do well

Research shows that when students learn together in mixed groups:
- Students who find maths harder don't fall further behind
- Students who are ahead don't get bored – they learn by explaining ideas to others
- Everyone benefits from hearing different ways of solving problems

### It's fairer

Streaming can accidentally lock students into a path early on. A child who struggles in Year 7 might stay in the lower group for years, even if they improve. Mixed-attainment teaching gives every student the chance to progress.

### It builds confidence

When students only learn with others at the same level, some feel they're "not good at maths." In mixed groups, they see that everyone finds some things tricky – and that's normal.

---

## How Will Teachers Make This Work?

Teachers won't just teach one lesson to everyone. Instead:

- **Different tasks** – students might work on the same problem but at different depths
- **Flexible grouping** – students work in different groups depending on the task
- **One-to-one support** – teachers and teaching assistants help students who need it most
- **Challenge for all** – students who grasp concepts quickly move on to harder problems

---

## What About My Child?

Your child will:
- Still get support tailored to their needs
- Work with a wider range of peers
- Have more chances to see that maths can be solved in different ways
- Build resilience and problem-solving skills

---

## How Can You Help at Home?

- **Encourage a growth mindset** – praise effort, not just correct answers ("You worked hard on that" rather than "You're so clever")
- **Show maths in everyday life** – cooking, shopping, sports all use maths
- **Don't say "I was never good at maths"** – children pick up on this and believe they can't be either
